newsitem.title: UK: Coats says dividend "sign of confidence".
newsitem.headline: Coats says dividend "sign of confidence".

text.p: Coats Viyella Plc chief executive Neville Bain said on Thursday that the decision to maintain its 1996 dividend was a "a sign of strong confidence for 1997."
The 8.8 pence per share payout was not not covered by earnings per share, which slipped to 6.7 pence from 13.4 pence in 1995.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Bain said the group's long-term aim continued to be to achieve "dividend increases equal to or above the rate of inflation while building cover over time."
Group finance director Kirk Stephenson told Reuters that the strengthening of sterling in the latter part of 1996 had had a "neutral impact on the profit and loss account."
However, he said that if current dollar levels were maintained for the rest of 1997, pre-tax profits would be reduced by between five and eight million stg.

Stephenson said he was also concerned about the competitiveness of UK manufacturing given the relative weakness of Euroepan currencies, noting that the British position "is not as good as it was a year ago." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
